sentences.text: Edgarosaurus is a genus of polycotylid plesiosaur that contains only one known species, E. muddi.
Druckenmiller estimated the total length of Edgarosaurus to be roughly 3.2 to 3.7 meters, while its cranium measures 47.5 centimeters long.
The animal possessed large, fang-like teeth, with each premaxilla containing either six or seven teeth.
Compared to its close relatives, Edgarosaurus had a shorter and more robust face, a pineal opening on the top of the skull, and a slightly longer neck with 26 vertebrae.

The front ends of the mandible halves are fused to form a symphysis with six tooth pairs, which is a low number for a polycotylid, and the neck and skull together comprised up to 45% of the animal's total length.
The lower arm bones were very short and wide, and the forelimb digits consist of seven, eleven, ten, and nine bones respectively for the first through fifth digits.
Unlike most plesiosaurs, Edgarosaurus possessed a pineal opening on the top of the skull.
Its mandible halves are fused at the front to form a symphysis with only six tooth pairs, a notably low count for this group.

The holotype specimen of Edgarosaurus was discovered in the Shell Creek Member of the Thermopolis Shale in the spring of 1993, and the species Edgarosaurus muddi was named in 2002 by Pat S. Druckenmiller.
Edgarosaurus was probably one of the most primitive polycotylids.

The type specimen was found in Early Cretaceous (Albian, approximately 105 million years ago) rocks in Montana, United States, where the location was covered by the shallow Western Interior Seaway known as the Niobrara Sea.
